title: Questions and Answers — Loyalty Premium on Class H Preferred Stock Dividends, Member Equities & Patronage
content:
A Member Equities & Patronage Class H Preferred Stock holding that has been held a long time, or that has a record of reinvesting, earns a loyalty premium on its quarterly dividend rate.

## The rule

The dividend loyalty premium rests on the holding's age and its reinvestment record: a holding issued at least 60 whole months before today and carrying at least 4 reinvested dividend entries earns 0.10 percentage point; a holding that meets exactly one of those two conditions earns 0.05 percentage point; a holding that meets neither earns no premium.

The premium is added, in percentage points, to the annual rate at which the quarterly dividend is figured, the sum being one annual rate applied once; the premium never acts on another part of the rate.

## Questions answered

**How is the age of the holding measured?** In whole months from the holding's issue date to today. A holding issued 59 whole months ago does not meet the age condition; one issued 60 whole months ago does.

**What counts as a reinvested dividend entry?** Each quarterly dividend booked to the holding as reinvested in additional shares. Three such entries do not meet the reinvestment condition; four do.

**What does a holding meeting both conditions earn?** 0.10 percentage point.

**And a holding meeting only one of them?** 0.05 percentage point, whichever of the two it meets.

## Condition table

| Issued at least 60 whole months before today | At least 4 reinvested dividend entries | Loyalty premium |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 0.10 percentage point |
| Yes | No | 0.05 percentage point |
| No | Yes | 0.05 percentage point |
| No | No | None |

**Hypothetical illustration.** A holding issued 72 whole months ago with 9 reinvested dividend entries earns 0.10 percentage point; on a hypothetical annual rate of 4.25 percent the dividend is figured at 4.35 percent.
